item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption investigated conduct involving a senior Canterbury-Bankstown Council manager and a former council contractor.
item.support:
This investigation by the NSW Independent Commission 
Against Corruption (“the Commission”) centred around 
the conduct of former senior Canterbury-Bankstown 
Council (Council) employee

item.text: The investigation examined alleged financial benefits linked to temporary-worker recruitment and assistance in obtaining council contracts.
item.support:

item.text: The Commission found serious corrupt conduct by the manager and former contractor in a recruitment scheme that provided the manager with about $208,000.
item.section: Corrupt conduct findings in relation to recruitment
item.support:
The Commission found that Mr Webb engaged in serious 
corrupt conduct in connection with the recruitment 
scheme

item.text: The Commission also found serious corrupt conduct by the former contractor and a construction company director involving payments for help in securing council projects.
item.section: Corrupt conduct findings in relation to procurement
item.support:
The Commission finds that Mr Cossu engaged in serious 
corrupt conduct in connection with the procurement 
arrangement

item.text: The Commission made 19 corruption-prevention recommendations covering recruitment checks, temporary-worker oversight, capital works procurement, contract variations and conflicts of interest.
item.support:
Chapter 6 of this report sets out the corruption risks 
identified by the Commission during the investigation and 
the basis for its corruption prevention recommendations.
